class_name: 自然発生-強制-ナイデハオカナイ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.canonical_surface: ないでなんかいられない
patterns.usage_note: Names a reaction the subject cannot suppress, nearly always the speaker's own feeling or an act driven by it (涙をこぼさずにはいられない, 心配せずにはいられない). The sibling ないではおかない points outward at what an event inevitably forces on someone else. する becomes せずにはいられない, and the なんか・など・だって insertions add exasperation.

examples.ruby: その手紙[てがみ]を読[よ]んで、涙[なみだ]をこぼさずにはいられなかった。
examples.english: Reading that letter, I just couldn't hold back the tears.

examples.ruby: 友[とも]だちが困[こま]っているのに、助[たす]けないでなんかいられないよ。
examples.english: My friend's having a hard time; there's no way I could just not help.

examples.ruby: 連絡[れんらく]が途絶[とだ]えたままなので、心配[しんぱい]せずにはいられません。
examples.english: With no word from them at all, I can't help worrying.

patterns.usage_note: Says a result is unavoidable: with an event or a causative verb as subject, the thing inevitably provokes the outcome (読者を泣かせずにはおかない); with a human subject it is a vow not to let the matter rest. The sibling ずにはいられない reports a feeling the speaker cannot suppress rather than something inflicted from outside. It belongs to formal written Japanese, and する becomes せずにはおかない.

examples.ruby: この判決[はんけつ]は社会[しゃかい]に大[おお]きな議論[ぎろん]を呼[よ]ばずにはおかない。
examples.english: This ruling is bound to touch off a major debate in society.

examples.ruby: この物語[ものがたり]の結末[けつまつ]は、読[よ]む者[もの]の心[こころ]を捉[とら]えないではおかない。
examples.english: The ending of this tale cannot fail to seize the reader's heart.

examples.ruby: 我々[われわれ]は不正[ふせい]の全容[ぜんよう]を明[あき]らかにせずにはおかない。
examples.english: We will not rest until the full extent of the misconduct is laid bare.
